newsitem.title: SWEDEN: NorScan pulp stocks rise a little in Aug-Momentum.
newsitem.headline: NorScan pulp stocks rise a little in Aug-Momentum.

text.p: Pulp stocks held by producers in North America and Scandinavia (NorScan) rose by 50,000 tonnes to reach 1.75 million tonnes at the end of August, pulp and paper consultancy group Momentum said on Friday.
Momentum said producer inventories fell by over 20,000 tonnes in the Nordic countries last month.
"(Stocks) rose only modestly by 10,000 tonnes in Canada and by 60,000 tonnes in the U.S.," Momentum said in a statement.
The consultant said shipments of chemical paper grades market pulp continued to be moderately strong in August, up slightly from July, at slightly below 90 percent of capacity.
Particularly strong shipments, 96 percent of capacity, were recorded for Canada where the bulk of the increase over July was in shipping to Europe.

"Otherwise the momentum holding up higher shipments than expected has been in the strong demand in Southeast Asia where inventories of purchased pulp are now estimated to be about one third above normal levels," it said.
Production was still running high compared to capacity in North America (96 percent) while much lower operating rates were recorded in the Nordic countries.

"Recent information is, however, indicating normal downtime (up to a week) in the U.S. during Labour day holiday (first week in September) and similarly in Canada with in some cases extended downtime to correct too high inventories," Momentum said.

It said considerable downtime was also taken during September through October in Sweden for various reasons including maintenance and rebuilding production units which could bring inventories to levels below normal.
